criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — MODERN AUDIO GRAPH FOR TRUE POSITIONAL 3D. World audio (footsteps, weapons, ambience, props) is built as an EXPLICITLY WIRED node graph — AudioPlayer -> Wire -> [optional effect nodes] -> AudioEmitter -> AudioListener -> AudioDeviceOutput — where audio flows through Wire instances (SourceInstance/TargetInstance), NOT the parent-child tree, with a tuned AudioEmitter distance/attenuation curve so position and falloff are real. The legacy-path equivalent that also passes: a Sound parented to an Attachment/Part in Workspace with a deliberately chosen RollOffMode (InverseTapered for natural falloff) and tuned RollOffMinDistance/MaxDistance sized to the source's role. The discriminator is whether the build commits to a routed/positioned spatial chain rather than a bare 2D Sound at defaults. PASS requires the build to state (1) for the modern path, the source->emitter->listener->output chain connected by Wire (a node with no outgoing Wire is silent — the #1 modern-API trap), OR for the legacy path, a Sound anchored to a Part/Attachment with a chosen RollOffMode + tuned min/max distance, AND (2) an attenuation/falloff intent matched to the source scale (a campfire heard at ~40 studs vs a siren that carries far) rather than one default rolloff on everything. A single Sound:Play() at default 2D/no spatialization, or an AudioPlayer parented to a part expecting sound with no Wire, FAILS. A correctly wired/anchored positional chain with role-sized attenuation PASSES; an explicit per-source DistanceAttenuation keypoint curve and a two-layer split (non-spatial music/UI routed AudioPlayer->AudioDeviceOutput directly while world sound goes through emitter/listener) push toward full marks. A spatial chain that exists but leaves rolloff/attenuation at defaults earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: Generic Roblox audio is a single Sound instance dropped on a Part at default properties — one monolithic object that bakes source, spatialization and output together, plays effectively 2D, and cannot be re-routed, bus-mixed, or have effects reordered. The modern node graph (AudioPlayer/Emitter/Listener/Output as discrete wired nodes) is the audio analog of the VFX 'multiple role-separated emitters vs one default ParticleEmitter' tell: separating the stages is what makes every other technique (effect chaining, bus mixing, ducking, directional audio, occlusion) physically expressible — a bare default Sound can do none of them. The #1 correctness trap is assuming parenting routes audio as it does for legacy Sound and getting silence; knowing the graph is silent-by-default without Wires, and sizing attenuation to the source, is the difference between 'a sound that happens to play' and audio that communicates distance and space. Grading the routed/anchored-with-tuned-falloff commitment keeps this discriminating: a wired positional chain (or a correctly anchored legacy Sound) clears it; a default 2D Sound cannot.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing EITHER (modern) AudioPlayer -> Wire -> AudioEmitter -> AudioListener -> AudioDeviceOutput with Wire SourceInstance/TargetInstance set so the chain is not silent, OR (legacy) a Sound parented to a Part/Attachment with a chosen RollOffMode (InverseTapered) + tuned RollOffMinDistance/MaxDistance — AND an attenuation/falloff sized to the source's role rather than one default rolloff everywhere. An explicit AudioEmitter.DistanceAttenuation keypoint curve, the AudioPlayer.AssetId 'rbxassetid://' full-form correctness, and a non-spatial-vs-spatial routing split are credited toward full marks. A single 2D Sound:Play(), or an AudioPlayer parented (not Wired) to a part, does NOT satisfy this; a routed/anchored chain left at default rolloff earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Build world sounds as a wired graph (AudioPlayer -> Wire -> AudioEmitter -> AudioListener -> AudioDeviceOutput) — remembering a node with no outgoing Wire is silent and AudioPlayer.AssetId needs the full 'rbxassetid://' prefix — or on the legacy path parent the Sound to an Attachment/Part with RollOffMode=InverseTapered and RollOffMin/MaxDistance sized to the source (tight for a UI prop, wide for a siren). Route non-spatial music/UI straight AudioPlayer->AudioDeviceOutput; spatialize only diegetic world sound.

grading.pass: The build commits to a positional spatial chain: EITHER (modern) a wired AudioPlayer -> Wire -> AudioEmitter -> AudioListener -> AudioDeviceOutput graph with Wire SourceInstance/TargetInstance set so the chain is not silent, OR (legacy) a Sound anchored to a Part/Attachment with a chosen RollOffMode (e.g. InverseTapered) and tuned RollOffMinDistance/MaxDistance — AND attenuation/falloff sized to each source's role rather than one default rolloff on everything. Full marks add an explicit DistanceAttenuation keypoint curve, full 'rbxassetid://' AssetId form, and a non-spatial-vs-spatial routing split.
grading.partial: A routed/anchored positional chain exists (modern wired graph or anchored legacy Sound) but rolloff/attenuation is left at defaults, OR a single rolloff is applied uniformly to all sources regardless of scale, so distance/falloff is not matched to source role.
grading.fail: A single Sound:Play() at default 2D / no spatialization, an AudioPlayer parented to a part with no Wire (silent), or any setup that bakes a bare default Sound with no positional routing and no tuned falloff.

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — DYNAMIC MIXING BUS HIERARCHY. Every sound is organized into a small named bus tree — Master -> {Music, SFX, Ambience, UI, Voice} (SoundGroups on the legacy path, or many AudioPlayers' Wires fanning into shared AudioFader/AudioDeviceOutput buses on the modern path), with SFX able to nest sub-buses (e.g. Footsteps) — and individual sources are kept at a NEUTRAL level so the buses do the balancing. The discriminator is whether the build commits to a category bus structure with disciplined gain staging rather than every Sound set to full Volume individually. PASS requires the build to state (1) a Master->category bus hierarchy where a parent group's volume cascades to children (so player settings sliders — mute music, keep SFX — and global balance are one property edit, not a per-sound script), AND (2) neutral source gain staging — individual Sound.Volume / AudioFader gain left around a neutral level and the buses doing the balancing, explicitly avoiding 'doubling up' (Sound 1.0 x group 1.0 x parent 1.0) that stacks gain and clips. (Note the legacy SoundGroup.Volume is a MULTIPLIER against each child's Volume, not a setter.) A build that sets Volume per-Sound individually with no grouping, no master/category control, and no settings sliders FAILS. A build that commits to the bus tree AND neutral gain staging PASSES; per-category player volume sliders and a concurrent-voice/voice-stealing cap (e.g. ~8 footstep / ~16 impact voices, stop oldest) push toward full marks. A build with a bus tree but everything still at full Volume (gain doubling/clipping), or grouping with no settings exposure, earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The generic build sets Volume per-Sound with no grouping, so there is no master/category control, no settings sliders, and balancing the mix means editing dozens of sounds by hand — and the classic 'everything at 0.5 or 1.0' clips when many loud sounds stack. A bus hierarchy is the single structural quality gate that makes mixing, ducking, and player audio settings possible at all — it is the SoundGroup-equivalent of the VFX 'performance budget' criterion: the organizing backbone every other mixing technique (ducking, bus FX, voice capping) composes onto. It is also a documented player complaint — joining games and having to mute them due to overwhelming/ear-piercing audio — that a bus tree plus per-category sliders directly fixes. Grading the bus-hierarchy-AND-neutral-gain-staging commitment keeps this discriminating: a budgeted bus mix clears it; a flat per-sound full-volume build cannot.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) a Master -> {Music/SFX/Ambience/UI/Voice} bus hierarchy (SoundGroups legacy, or AudioFader/shared-output buses modern) where parent volume cascades to children, AND (2) neutral source levels with the buses doing the balance, explicitly avoiding gain doubling (source 1.0 x group 1.0 x parent 1.0 = clipping). Per-category player volume sliders, an AudioFader-is-where-volume-lives note (AudioPlayer has no Volume property), and a concurrent-voice/voice-stealing cap are credited toward full marks. Per-Sound individual Volume with no grouping, no master control and no sliders does NOT satisfy this; a bus tree left at full source Volume, or grouping with no settings exposure, earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Create a SoundService bus tree (Master > Music / SFX / Ambience / UI / Voice), assign every Sound.SoundGroup (or fan AudioPlayer Wires into shared AudioFader buses), keep each source at a neutral ~0.5 and let the groups balance, expose per-category volume sliders to players, and cap concurrent voices per category (stop the oldest past the limit) so dense moments don't clip or stutter on mobile.

grading.pass: The build commits to a Master -> {Music/SFX/Ambience/UI/Voice} bus tree (SoundGroups legacy, or AudioFader/shared-output buses modern) where parent volume cascades to children, AND keeps individual sources at a neutral level letting the buses balance, explicitly avoiding gain doubling (source x group x parent stacking to clipping). Full marks add per-category player volume sliders, the AudioFader-is-where-volume-lives note, and a concurrent-voice/voice-stealing cap.
grading.partial: A category bus tree exists but every source is still at full Volume (gain doubling/clipping risk), OR grouping is present with no master/settings exposure (no sliders, no cascading control) — one half of the structure without the disciplined gain staging or the player-facing control.
grading.fail: Volume is set per-Sound individually with no grouping, no Master/category control, and no settings sliders — a flat per-sound full-volume mix with no bus structure.

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — CURATED LIBRARY USE WITH LAYERED + RANDOMIZED VARIATION. Repeated SFX (footsteps, impacts, gunshots, UI) and key one-shots use DELIBERATELY-CHOSEN, role/tone-matched Creator-Store/Toolbox assets (not one placeholder clip), AND every repeated trigger is de-repeated: a pool of multiple alternate clips picked at random PLUS per-play PlaybackSpeed/pitch (~+/-5%) and slight volume jitter, so the same waveform is never heard identically. The discriminator is whether the build commits to BOTH curated fit AND per-instance variation. PASS requires the build to state (1) fitting, intentionally-selected library assets matched to the event's role/tone from clean-license sources ('free' is a price, not a license — reject re-uploads), with length matched to use (30s+ for loops, short for one-shots), AND (2) for any repeated sound, a pool of 4-8 variant clips chosen at random PLUS per-trigger pitch/volume jitter — explicitly breaking the 'machine-gun'/looped-clip artifact (pools should be material/context-specific where it matters, e.g. per-surface footsteps). A build that retriggers ONE fixed asset id at one fixed pitch on every footstep/hit, or grabs the first keyword-matched Toolbox clip, FAILS. A build that commits to curated fit AND a random pool + pitch/volume jitter PASSES; per-material footstep pools, layered combat hits (swing/whoosh + impact + victim reaction as 3 clips), and avoiding the replay-same-index bug push toward full marks. A build that pools/jitters but the clips are mismatched/placeholder, or curates well but replays a single clip identically, earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The generic default is one Sound asset id retriggered identically — the ear detects the identical waveform instantly and it reads as cheap; or it is the first keyword-matched (often re-uploaded, tone-mismatched) Toolbox grab played at defaults. A single fixed sample at fixed pitch on every footstep/hit is THE recognizable amateur audio tell, the exact audio analog of VFX 'constant Size/Transparency' and 'synchronized particle death' — pros say 'if your footsteps sound right, your sound system is built right.' Since the agent CURATES rather than authors audio, the quality of the asset-id selection is upstream of everything, and a random pool + micro pitch/volume jitter is the cheapest, highest-impact upgrade — pure curation+scripting, the project's curate-don't-author mandate. Layering a combat hit into swing+impact+reaction (vs one flat sample) gives blows weight the same way. Grading curated-fit-AND-de-repetition keeps this discriminating: a varied, fitting pool clears it; a single-clip-at-one-pitch (or a placeholder grab) cannot.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) role/tone-matched, clean-license library assets chosen deliberately per event with length matched to use (not one placeholder/first-result clip), AND (2) for repeated sounds, a pool of 4-8 variant clips selected at random PLUS per-play PlaybackSpeed/pitch (~+/-5%) and slight volume jitter. Per-material footstep pools, 3-clip layered combat hits (swing + impact + reaction), and explicitly avoiding the replay-same-index-before-cycling bug are credited toward full marks. One fixed asset id retriggered at one pitch, or a first-keyword Toolbox grab at defaults, does NOT satisfy this; pooling/jitter on mismatched clips, or good curation that still replays a single clip, earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Pick fitting, clean-license library clips per event (right length for the role, atmosphere keywords/exclusions to find the right asset id), then for every repeated sound pool 4-8 variants (per-surface for footsteps), pick at random, and randomize PlaybackSpeed/pitch ~+/-5% plus slight volume per play — and layer key combat hits as swing/whoosh + impact + victim-reaction — so no two triggers sound identical.

grading.pass: The build commits to BOTH curated fit AND per-instance variation: (1) deliberately-selected, role/tone-matched, clean-license library assets with length matched to use, AND (2) for every repeated sound a pool of 4-8 variant clips picked at random plus per-play PlaybackSpeed/pitch (~+/-5%) and volume jitter so the same waveform is never heard identically. Full marks add per-material footstep pools, 3-clip layered combat hits (swing + impact + reaction), and avoiding the replay-same-index bug.
grading.partial: Only one side is satisfied: the build pools/jitters but the clips are mismatched/placeholder, OR it curates fitting clips well but still replays a single clip identically with no random pool or pitch/volume jitter.
grading.fail: One fixed asset id is retriggered at one fixed pitch on every footstep/hit, OR the build grabs the first keyword-matched Toolbox clip and plays it at defaults — no curation discipline and no de-repetition.

criteria.statement: Sounds are triggered by an EVENT-TO-SOURCE BINDING SYSTEM, not by playing a clip in a vacuum. The discriminator is whether the build commits to a wiring discipline where (a) SFX fire as precise one-shots driven off real gameplay/animation events — Touched / Humanoid step / weapon fire / objective complete, and at the high end animation event markers via AnimationTrack:GetMarkerReachedSignal so audio lands on the exact frame — AND (b) the emitting node (AudioEmitter or Sound) RIDES the actual moving instance (foot Motor6D, blade Attachment, projectile) so the trigger and the spatial origin are the SAME object, rather than a 2D Sound:Play() that has no source at all or a clip pinned to a fixed world position / HumanoidRootPart center. PASS requires the build to state BOTH (1) event-accurate one-shot triggering on named gameplay or animation events (not a Looped always-on drone, not an untimed clip), AND (2) that the sound is emitted from a positional node attached to the moving source (any AudioEmitter/anchored-Sound chain counts as the source-bound origin) so it reads directionally and follows the actor. A single 2D Sound:Play() with no AudioEmitter and no anchored origin — firing on an event but from nowhere/everywhere — FAILS, because event timing without a bound source is exactly the generic pattern. A build that names event-marker-synced one-shots emitted from a positional/source-bound node PASSES; binding to the specific limb/tool (not HRP), a debounce against retrigger spam, and one-shot cleanup on the Ended signal push toward full marks. A build that fires on events but is explicitly 2D/non-spatial with no emitter or anchored origin earns FAIL (not partial) — the source binding is the load-bearing half this criterion grades and a non-spatial clip provides none of it; partial is reserved for a build that binds to a positional source but loops always-on or omits the debounce/cleanup.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The original criterion graded event-firing and source-binding as two equally-weighted prongs, so a 2D Sound that merely 'fired on every event' scored PARTIAL — the same grade a strong systems artifact earned — because both lacked the lifecycle hygiene details (debounce, cleanup). That collapsed the gap. The real above-generic tell is whether the trigger and the spatial origin are the SAME moving object: generic audio plays a sourceless 2D clip on an event (timing only, no place), while a real system wires the emit to a positional node that rides the actor so footsteps come from the feet and a swing comes from the blade. By making 'event one-shot emitted from a positional source-bound node' the conjunctive PASS gate and explicitly scoring a non-spatial event clip as FAIL, the bare 2D-Sound build can no longer reach partial, while an artifact that commits to event-marker-synced one-shots through an AudioEmitter chain clears the bar; the limb-vs-HRP precision and Ended cleanup move to full-marks pushers where they belong.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing BOTH (1) SFX fired as one-shots on named gameplay or animation events (Touched, Humanoid step, weapon fire, objective complete, ideally AnimationTrack:GetMarkerReachedSignal frame-accurate markers) — NOT a Looped always-on Sound and NOT an untimed clip — AND (2) the sound emitted from a positional node bound to a moving source (an AudioEmitter wired into the chain, or a Sound parented to the moving Part/Attachment) so the origin follows the actor rather than being a 2D/sourceless Sound:Play() or a clip pinned to a fixed world position. Binding to the specific limb/tool rather than HumanoidRootPart, a debounce (set flag / Play / await Ended / clear), and destroying one-shot instances on Ended are credited toward full marks. A 2D Sound that fires on events but has no AudioEmitter and no anchored origin does NOT satisfy this and earns FAIL; a positional source-bound emitter that nonetheless loops always-on or omits debounce/cleanup earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Drive every SFX off the real event (Touched / Humanoid step / weapon fire, and animation markers via GetMarkerReachedSignal so footsteps and swings hit the exact frame) and emit it from a positional node bound to the moving source — an AudioEmitter wired into the chain (or a Sound parented to the foot Motor6D / blade Attachment), never a sourceless 2D Sound:Play() or a clip pinned to a fixed world position / HumanoidRootPart. Add a debounce against retrigger spam and destroy one-shot instances on the Ended signal.

grading.pass: The build commits to event-to-source binding: (1) one-shots fired on named gameplay/animation events (Touched, Humanoid step, weapon fire, objective complete, ideally GetMarkerReachedSignal markers), NOT a Looped always-on drone or untimed clip, AND (2) the sound emitted from a positional node bound to the moving source (an AudioEmitter wired into the chain, or a Sound parented to the moving Part/Attachment) so the origin follows the actor. Full marks add binding to the specific limb/tool rather than HumanoidRootPart, a debounce against retrigger spam, and one-shot cleanup on Ended.
grading.partial: The build emits from a positional source-bound node but loops always-on with no event timing, OR fires on correct events from a bound positional source but omits the debounce/cleanup hygiene — one structural half present, the other (event timing or lifecycle) missing.
grading.fail: A 2D/non-spatial Sound:Play() with no AudioEmitter and no anchored origin (event timing but no source binding — the generic pattern), a Looped Sound left always-on, or a clip hardcoded to a fixed world position / HumanoidRootPart center.

criteria.change_reason: Original failed to discriminate: MEAN scored PARTIAL ('fires on every event') and GREAT also scored PARTIAL, so the criterion separated nothing. The cause was treating event-firing as enough for partial credit regardless of whether the sound had ANY spatial source. Rewrite makes the conjunctive PASS gate 'event one-shot EMITTED FROM A POSITIONAL SOURCE-BOUND NODE' and explicitly downgrades a non-spatial event clip from partial to FAIL — so the bare 2D Sound (no emitter, no origin) can no longer reach partial, while the GREAT artifact's 'event-marker-synced one-shots' through its AudioEmitter chain now clears partial/pass. Limb-vs-HRP precision, debounce, and Ended cleanup are demoted to full-marks pushers so the absence of those niche details no longer drags a real systems build down to the same grade as the generic one.

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — SIDECHAIN DUCKING + MASTER DYNAMICS. The music/ambient bus automatically drops under key SFX/dialogue via a sidechained AudioCompressor (the music bus on the Input pin, the voice/critical-SFX bus on the SidechainInput/Sidechain pin) — NOT by manually tweening every music Sound's Volume on each event — and the master output carries a brick-wall AudioLimiter so dense moments never clip. The discriminator is whether the build commits to signal-level automatic ducking AND a master safety ceiling, rather than per-event volume hacks at full level. PASS requires the build to state (1) a sidechain duck: AudioCompressor with Input = music bus and Sidechain = voice/important-SFX bus, with tuned Threshold / Ratio / fast Attack / slow Release / MakeupGain so music breathes around speech/combat automatically (legacy equivalent: a CompressorSoundEffect ducking one SoundGroup from another), AND (2) an AudioLimiter on the master with a set MaxLevel as the instant-response hard ceiling (vs the compressor's gradual curve) so summed voices never distort. A build that tweens each music Volume per dialogue event, or leaves every Sound at full Volume with no master limiter, FAILS. A build that commits to sidechain ducking AND a master limiter PASSES; tuned Attack/Release shaping, a deliberate effect-chain ORDER (EQ -> Compressor -> Reverb/Echo send -> Fader -> Limiter last), and per-context volume automation push toward full marks. A build with ducking but no master limiter (or a limiter but script-tweened ducking) earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The naive approach — tweening every music Sound's Volume in a script on each dialogue/SFX event — is 'both ugly and unreliable,' snaps audibly, and doesn't scale to many players in different states. A sidechained compressor makes music breathe around dialogue/criticals automatically at the signal level (deterministic, per-sample, DAW-grade, invisible-when-done-right — how pro mixes keep speech intelligible), and only the modern Audio API can do it cleanly: a clear modern-vs-legacy advantage. A master AudioLimiter responds INSTANTLY to keep the stream below MaxLevel (unlike a compressor's gradual response) and is the safety net for the exact clipping the audio-balance critiques describe; getting the effect-chain ORDER right (limiter LAST) is what stops a busy mix turning to mud — the audio analog of VFX ZOffset draw-order. Grading the sidechain-duck-AND-master-limiter commitment keeps this discriminating: a self-ducking, limited mix clears it; a per-event-tween, no-ceiling build cannot.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) a sidechained AudioCompressor — Input = music/ambient bus, Sidechain = voice/important-SFX bus — with tuned Threshold/Ratio/fast-Attack/slow-Release/MakeupGain (or a legacy CompressorSoundEffect ducking one SoundGroup from another), AND (2) an AudioLimiter on the master with a set MaxLevel as an instant hard ceiling. A deliberate effect-chain order (EQ -> Compressor -> Reverb/Echo send -> Fader -> Limiter last) and per-context volume automation are credited toward full marks. Per-event Volume tweening of each music Sound, or full-level sources with no master limiter, does NOT satisfy this; ducking without a master limiter, or a limiter with only script-tweened ducking, earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Wire the music bus into an AudioCompressor's Input and the voice/critical-SFX bus into its Sidechain pin (fast Attack so the duck is responsive, slow Release so music swells back, MakeupGain to restore loudness) — legacy: a CompressorSoundEffect ducking one SoundGroup from another — and put an AudioLimiter with a set MaxLevel last on the master so layered combat+music+voice never clips, ordering the chain EQ -> Compressor -> Reverb/Echo -> Fader -> Limiter.

grading.pass: The build commits to signal-level automatic ducking AND a master safety ceiling: (1) a sidechained AudioCompressor with Input = music/ambient bus and Sidechain = voice/critical-SFX bus, tuned Threshold/Ratio/fast-Attack/slow-Release/MakeupGain (or legacy CompressorSoundEffect ducking one SoundGroup from another), AND (2) an AudioLimiter on the master with a set MaxLevel as an instant hard ceiling. Full marks add a deliberate effect-chain order (EQ -> Compressor -> Reverb/Echo -> Fader -> Limiter last) and per-context volume automation.
grading.partial: Only one side holds: the build has sidechain ducking but no master limiter, OR has a master limiter but achieves ducking only via script-tweened music volume rather than a signal-level sidechain.
grading.fail: The build tweens each music Sound's Volume per dialogue/SFX event, or leaves every source at full Volume with no master limiter — brittle per-event volume hacks and no safety ceiling.

criteria.statement: Spatial sources express SHAPE — facing and physical size — not just distance. The discriminator is whether the build commits to a spatial-emission model that goes BEYOND an omnidirectional point with one distance rolloff: at minimum it must articulate a deliberate per-source ATTENUATION/EMISSION PROFILE (the falloff curve sized to each source's role and scale — a 40-stud campfire vs a far-carrying siren vs a wide waterfall), and the ceiling adds true directional or volumetric emission via AudioEmitter/AudioListener AngleAttenuation cones (loudspeaker / megaphone / PA / directional alarm) and/or SoundService.VolumetricAudio explicitly Enabled for large surfaces. PASS requires the build to state (1) a positional emitter chain whose attenuation/falloff is deliberately SHAPED per source — distinct curves matched to source scale/role rather than one default rolloff stamped on everything — establishing that emission shape is a modeled dimension, NOT merely that sounds are 3D. A build where every source is an omnidirectional point at the SAME default rolloff (including a bare 2D Sound with no rolloff at all), so a PA horn sounds identical from behind and a 50-stud waterfall collapses to a pinprick, FAILS. A build committing to role-sized per-source attenuation curves PASSES; naming an explicit AngleAttenuation directional cone for a facing-dependent source OR VolumetricAudio (explicitly Enabled, not Automatic) with surface-measured rolloff for a wide source pushes toward full marks. A build that names 'tuned attenuation curves' as a system but does not differentiate them per source role earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The original criterion required the narrow named features AngleAttenuation OR VolumetricAudio as the PASS gate. A strong general 'pro audio system' artifact that commits to 'tuned attenuation curves' but never enumerates those two specific APIs failed exactly like the bare 2D-Sound build — both omit the keyword — so the criterion separated nothing (MEAN fail, GREAT fail). The genuine above-generic boundary is one step lower and far more discriminating: does the build model emission SHAPE at all (per-source falloff curves sized to role) versus stamping one omnidirectional default rolloff (or no rolloff) on everything? Generic audio is one rolloff everywhere; a real system shapes attenuation per source and, at the ceiling, adds cones/volume. Making role-sized per-source attenuation the PASS gate lets the GREAT artifact's 'tuned attenuation curves' clear it while the MEAN artifact's '2D and non-spatial, no RollOff' build cannot, and keeps AngleAttenuation/VolumetricAudio as the full-marks ceiling they are.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing a positional emitter chain whose attenuation/falloff is deliberately SHAPED per source — distinct curves/distances matched to each source's scale and role (e.g. a tight campfire vs a far-carrying siren vs a wide machine) rather than one default rolloff applied uniformly, OR no rolloff at all. Naming an explicit AudioEmitter/AudioListener AngleAttenuation directional cone for a facing-dependent source (loudspeaker, megaphone, PA, directional alarm, shotgun/figure-8 mic), and/or SoundService.VolumetricAudio explicitly Enabled (not Automatic) with surface-measured rolloff for a large source (waterfall, river, force field, big machine), are credited toward full marks. Every source as an omnidirectional point at the same default rolloff — or a 2D Sound with no rolloff — does NOT satisfy this and earns FAIL; 'tuned attenuation curves' asserted as a system but not differentiated per source role earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Shape attenuation per source instead of one default rolloff everywhere: size each emitter's falloff curve / min-max distance to the source's role and scale (tight for a UI prop, wide for a siren, surface-sized for a waterfall). Then for facing-dependent sources add an AudioEmitter.AngleAttenuation cone (loud in front, quiet behind) — and/or an AudioListener cone for a directional mic — and enable SoundService.VolumetricAudio (explicitly Enabled, not Automatic) on large surfaces so they emit from the whole body with rolloff measured from the surface.

grading.pass: The build models emission shape: a positional emitter chain whose attenuation/falloff is deliberately shaped per source — distinct curves/distances matched to each source's scale and role rather than one default rolloff on everything. Full marks add an explicit AngleAttenuation directional cone for a facing-dependent source (loudspeaker, megaphone, PA, directional alarm) and/or VolumetricAudio explicitly Enabled with surface-measured rolloff for a large source (waterfall, river, big machine).
grading.partial: The build names 'tuned attenuation curves' or a positional chain as a system but does not differentiate the curves per source role/scale (one curve approach asserted but not sized to individual sources), so emission shape is claimed but not demonstrably modeled per source.
grading.fail: Every source is an omnidirectional point at the same default rolloff — including a bare 2D/non-spatial Sound with no RollOff — so a PA horn sounds identical from behind and a wide source collapses to a pinprick; no per-source attenuation shaping, no cone, no volumetric emission.

criteria.change_reason: Original failed to discriminate: both MEAN and GREAT scored FAIL because the PASS gate demanded the narrow named APIs (AngleAttenuation / VolumetricAudio) that even the strong systems artifact ('tuned attenuation curves', 'true 3D positional audio') never explicitly enumerated. Rewrite lowers the PASS gate to the genuinely discriminating commitment — deliberate per-source attenuation SHAPING sized to role, versus one omnidirectional default rolloff / no rolloff — which the GREAT artifact's 'tuned attenuation curves' satisfies and the MEAN artifact's '2D and non-spatial, no RollOff' provably does not. The directional-cone and volumetric-emission features are preserved as the full-marks ceiling, so the criterion now rewards the systems commitment the great build actually made while still failing the generic one.

criteria.statement: The audio system declares WHERE the listener lives and HOW self-audio reaches the player, rather than leaving both to engine defaults. The discriminator is whether the build commits to BOTH (a) a deliberate AudioListener PLACEMENT decision — the listener bound to a chosen origin (character/head, via SoundService.DefaultListenerLocation or a listener parented to the head Motor6D) so directional cues are correct, instead of an implicit camera-default or no listener at all — AND (b) a latency-aware self-audio model where the local player's OWN action SFX (gun, footstep, hit-confirm, UI) are played CLIENT-SIDE for instant 0ms feedback while the server authoritatively replicates the event to remote players (acknowledging ~80-120ms). PASS requires the build to state (1) a deliberate listener origin (DefaultListenerLocation set, or AudioListener placed on the head/character — NOT 'every source is 2D with no listener' and NOT relying on the unspoken camera default), AND (2) that self-audio is predicted on the client for immediate feedback with server authority for others. A build that has no AudioListener at all (pure 2D audio) or never states a listener origin, AND plays all audio without a client-prediction/server-authority split, FAILS — defaulting both decisions is the generic pattern. A build that places the listener deliberately AND predicts self-audio client-side PASSES; ContentProvider:PreloadAsync of only short time-critical one-shots while streaming long music/ambience pushes toward full marks. A build that wires an AudioListener into the chain but never states WHERE it is placed or whether self-audio is predicted earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The original criterion required both client-prediction netcode AND head-Motor6D listener placement as a conjunctive PASS gate, and graded a build that merely names 'AudioListener' as a chain node but specifies neither as FAIL — the same grade as the bare 2D build with no listener at all. That collapsed two very different artifacts to one grade. But the genuinely discriminating fact is still present: the MEAN build has NO AudioListener whatsoever (pure 2D), while the GREAT build wires an AudioListener into its chain — it just doesn't state placement or prediction. Rather than reward a chain node that says nothing about the two real decisions, the rewrite keeps the conjunctive PASS (placement + prediction are the actual above-generic moves) but sharpens the partial/fail boundary: a build with NO listener and NO prediction split (MEAN) fails; a build that at least commits a listener into the graph but leaves placement/prediction unstated (GREAT, today) lands at partial — separating them — and a build that nails both clears pass. This restores a three-way ordering instead of flattening MEAN and GREAT to the same FAIL.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing BOTH (1) a deliberate AudioListener placement — SoundService.DefaultListenerLocation set, or an AudioListener parented to the head Motor6D / character (not an implicit camera default, not 'no listener / all 2D') — AND (2) the local player's own action SFX predicted client-side for 0ms feedback while the server authoritatively replicates the event to remote players (acknowledging ~80-120ms latency). ContentProvider:PreloadAsync of only short time-critical one-shots while streaming long ambience/music is credited toward full marks. A build with no AudioListener at all and no client-prediction/server-authority split does NOT satisfy this and earns FAIL; a build that wires an AudioListener into the chain but states neither its placement nor a self-audio prediction model earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Declare the listener origin — set SoundService.DefaultListenerLocation=Character or parent the AudioListener to the head Motor6D (not the camera) so head-turns give correct directional cues — and play the local player's own action SFX (gun, footstep, hit-confirm, UI) on the client instantly for 0ms feedback while the server validates and replicates to others. Preload only the short time-critical one-shots and stream long music/ambience on demand.

grading.pass: The build commits to BOTH: (1) a deliberate AudioListener origin — DefaultListenerLocation set, or the listener on the head Motor6D / character (not camera-default, not absent) — AND (2) own action SFX predicted client-side for 0ms feedback while the server authoritatively replicates to remote players. Full marks add ContentProvider:PreloadAsync of only short time-critical one-shots while streaming long music/ambience.
grading.partial: The build wires an AudioListener into the audio graph (a listener exists in the chain) but never states WHERE it is placed (head/character vs camera) OR whether self-audio is client-predicted vs server-authoritative — a listener is present but the two load-bearing decisions are unstated.
grading.fail: No AudioListener at all (pure 2D audio) or no listener origin ever named, AND no client-prediction/server-authority split for self-audio — both decisions left to defaults, the generic pattern.

criteria.change_reason: Original failed to discriminate: both MEAN and GREAT scored FAIL — MEAN because it has no listener and no netcode, GREAT because, although it wires an AudioListener into its chain, it never states placement or prediction, and the original graded that as fail too. Rewrite keeps placement+prediction as the conjunctive PASS (the real above-generic moves) but moves the partial/fail line so the two artifacts separate: a build with NO listener and NO prediction split (MEAN) stays FAIL, while a build that at least commits an AudioListener into the graph but leaves placement/prediction unstated (GREAT) now earns PARTIAL. That gives MEAN < GREAT instead of MEAN = GREAT, while still reserving PASS for the build that actually states a head/character listener origin and client-predicted self-audio.

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — MULTI-SOURCE CONTINUOUS SOUNDSCAPE WITH DISTINCT ROUTED ROLES (not one monolithic clip). The build's audio is composed of MULTIPLE concurrently-active, role-separated sound sources — at minimum a continuous/looping bed layer AND event-driven SFX AND music — each routed to its own named category so the soundscape is a layered mix rather than a single clip retriggered. The discriminator is whether the build commits to several simultaneously-playing, independently-routed audio roles (music vs SFX vs ambience vs UI, each on its own SoundGroup/AudioFader bus or its own emitter chain) versus ONE sound object that plays in isolation on each event. PASS requires the build to state (1) at least THREE distinct, concurrently-live source roles — e.g. a looping ambience/music bed that runs continuously UNDER event-fired SFX UNDER UI sound — each addressed as its own routed entity (named bus/group OR its own AudioPlayer chain), AND (2) that these roles coexist and mix simultaneously (a continuous layer playing WHILE one-shots fire), not a single Sound:Play() that is the only thing audible at any moment. A build that is a single 2D Sound:Play() reused for every event — one source, one role, no continuous bed, no concurrent layering — FAILS. A build that commits to a multi-role routed soundscape (bed + SFX + music/UI on separate buses/chains) PASSES; per-context scoping with AudioInteractionGroup (matching strings on AudioEmitter/AudioListener) to isolate teams/lobbies/instanced encounters/spectator/private channels, framed as the clean replacement for ReplicatedStorage-folder parenting hacks, pushes toward full marks. A build that names two roles or routes some audio but still collapses most events onto one shared generic source earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The original criterion only bit when a build had BOTH a spatial emitter/listener graph AND multiple sessions/teams — a structural pre-condition that neither a generic 2D build nor a strong-but-single-context build satisfies, so it scored N/A or fail on both and separated nothing. The genuinely discriminating, always-present fact one tier down is whether the build is a LAYERED multi-source soundscape at all: a generic build is literally one Sound object retriggered (the same monolithic clip is the entire audio system — no continuous bed, no concurrent roles, nothing mixes), whereas a real audio system runs several independently-routed sources at once (an ambience bed under event SFX under music/UI), which is the structural precondition every higher technique (bus mixing, ducking, per-role attenuation, and indeed interaction-group scoping) composes onto. This is the audio analog of the VFX 'multiple role-separated emitters vs one default ParticleEmitter' tell. Grading the multi-role-concurrent-routing commitment keeps it discriminating: a layered bus-routed soundscape clears it; a single 2D Sound:Play() reused everywhere cannot. AudioInteractionGroup per-context isolation is preserved as the full-marks ceiling, where it is a genuine differentiator only when multiple scopes exist.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) at least THREE distinct concurrently-live audio roles — a continuous/looping bed (ambience or music) running UNDER event-fired SFX and UNDER UI/music — each routed as its own entity (a named SoundGroup/AudioFader bus, e.g. Music/SFX/Ambience/UI, OR its own AudioPlayer->emitter chain), AND (2) that these layers coexist and mix at the same time (the bed keeps playing while one-shots fire), NOT a single Sound:Play() that is the only audible source per event. Matching AudioInteractionGroup strings on AudioEmitters/AudioListeners scoping audio per a named context (team/lobby/instanced encounter/spectator/private channel), framed as replacing per-player ReplicatedStorage-folder isolation, are credited toward full marks. A single 2D Sound reused for every event, one role only, no continuous bed, does NOT satisfy this and earns FAIL; naming two roles or routing some audio while most events still share one generic source earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Stop playing one Sound object on every event. Build the soundscape as several concurrently-live, separately-routed roles — a continuous looping ambience/music bed under event-driven SFX under UI sound — each on its own SoundGroup/AudioFader bus (Music/SFX/Ambience/UI) or its own AudioPlayer emitter chain, so the layers mix simultaneously instead of one clip being the entire audio system. If the build has multiple audio scopes (teams, lobbies, instanced dungeons, spectator, a private/party channel), scope them with matching AudioInteractionGroup strings on the emitters and listeners that should share audio (replacing per-player ReplicatedStorage-folder parenting hacks).

grading.pass: The build commits to a layered multi-source soundscape: (1) at least THREE distinct concurrently-live roles — a continuous/looping bed (ambience or music) under event-fired SFX under UI/music — each routed as its own named bus/group or its own emitter chain, AND (2) the roles coexist and mix simultaneously (the bed plays while one-shots fire), not a single Sound:Play() per event. Full marks add AudioInteractionGroup scoping (matching strings on AudioEmitters/AudioListeners) to isolate a named context (team/lobby/instanced encounter/spectator/private channel), framed as the clean replacement for ReplicatedStorage-folder parenting hacks.
grading.partial: A partial layering: the build names two concurrent roles or routes some audio to separate buses/chains, but most events still collapse onto one shared generic source and there is no clear continuous-bed-under-concurrent-one-shots structure (one half of the multi-role mix without full role separation).
grading.fail: A single 2D Sound:Play() reused for every event — one source, one role, no continuous bed, no concurrent layering — or audio that is otherwise a single monolithic clip with nothing else mixing alongside it.

criteria.change_reason: Original failed to discriminate: MEAN scored fail and GREAT scored n/a, so the criterion separated nothing — and worse, it only bit when a build had BOTH a spatial emitter/listener graph AND multiple sessions/teams, a precondition neither artifact met (GREAT has a spatial graph but no separate scopes => N/A; MEAN is pure 2D => excluded), so it was structurally incapable of ordering these two artifacts. Rewrite drops session-isolation as the PASS gate and retargets the criterion at the genuinely always-present, discriminating fact one tier down: whether the build is a LAYERED multi-source routed soundscape (continuous bed + concurrent SFX + music/UI on separate buses/chains) versus one monolithic 2D Sound:Play() reused per event. The GREAT artifact's 'SoundGroup/AudioFader bus hierarchy (SFX/Music/Ambient/UI)' plus its continuous adaptive-music bed and event one-shots clearly satisfies the three-concurrent-role gate; the MEAN artifact's single full-Volume 2D clip provably does not. AudioInteractionGroup per-context scoping is demoted to a full-marks pusher, where it is a real differentiator only when multiple scopes actually exist — so the criterion now produces MEAN(fail) < GREAT(pass) instead of a non-discriminating fail/n-a pair.

criteria.statement: CONTINUOUS / SUSTAINED-BED AUDIO STRATEGY (loops that run under gameplay, not one-shots fired in a vacuum). The build relies on at least one deliberately CONTINUOUS or sustained audio layer — a looping ambience/room-tone bed, an adaptive-music bed, an engine/drone, or a steady tonal layer — that plays underneath gameplay across time, rather than only firing a single clip per discrete event. The discriminator is whether the build commits to sustained/looping audio as a designed system element AT ALL (a bed that persists and is intended to be heard continuously) versus a build whose entire audio output is one clip retriggered on each event with no continuous layer. PASS requires the build to state (1) at least one continuous/looping/sustained audio layer that runs under gameplay (ambient bed, looping music, drone, or adaptive-music stems that sustain across states), AND (2) that this looping layer is treated as a crafted continuous element — given a deliberate length/role and intended to play seamlessly underneath, not a discrete one-shot. A build whose audio is a single non-looped clip played per event, with NO continuous/sustained layer of any kind, FAILS. A build that commits to a sustained looping bed/music layer running under gameplay PASSES; loop-seam integrity (cut at a zero-crossing on both channels and overlap-crossfaded so it does not click) AND format/length discipline (OGG not MP3 to avoid the leading-silence padding click, ~15s+ ambient beds / ~6-10s steady sounds) push toward full marks. A build that has a continuous looping layer but says nothing about seam integrity or format/length discipline earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The original criterion graded only the narrow loop-SEAM craft (zero-crossing cut, OGG-not-MP3 padding, both-channels) as its PASS gate. Neither artifact named those specifics, so both scored fail and it separated nothing — even though one build has a rich continuous-audio strategy (adaptive layered music whose stems crossfade by game state, plus ambient beds) and the other has literally zero sustained audio (a single non-looped clip per event). The genuinely discriminating, always-present fact one tier down is whether the build commits to ANY continuous/sustained looping layer at all — the structural precondition that loop-seam craft, adaptive music, and ambience beds all presuppose. A generic build is all one-shots in a vacuum (no bed ever persists); a real audio system always has something sustaining underneath. Making 'has a deliberately continuous/looping/sustained layer' the PASS gate lets the strong artifact's adaptive-music-bed-plus-ambience commitment clear it while the single-non-looped-clip build cannot, and preserves the actual seam/format craft as the full-marks ceiling where it belongs.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) at least one continuous/looping/sustained audio layer that runs under gameplay — a looping ambience/room-tone bed, looping or adaptive-stem music that sustains across states, an engine/drone, or a steady tonal layer — NOT only discrete one-shots fired per event, AND (2) that this layer is treated as a crafted continuous element with a deliberate role/length, intended to play seamlessly underneath. A clean loop seam (zero-crossing cut on both stereo channels, overlap-crossfaded so it does not click), OGG-not-MP3 (MP3 leading-silence padding clicks every loop), and length matched to role (~15s+ ambient beds, ~6-10s steady sounds) — including naming the MP3-padding click cause — are credited toward full marks. A single non-looped clip played per event with no sustained/continuous layer of any kind does NOT satisfy this and earns FAIL; a continuous looping layer present but with no statement of seam integrity or format/length discipline earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Give the soundscape at least one continuous, sustained layer that runs under gameplay — a looping ambience/room-tone bed, looping or adaptive-stem music, or an engine drone — instead of only firing one clip per event into silence. Then craft that loop so it is genuinely seamless: cut the loop point at a zero-crossing (both channels for stereo) and overlap-crossfade it so it doesn't click, use OGG not MP3 (MP3's leading-silence padding clicks every loop), and match length to role (~15s+ ambient beds, ~6-10s steady sounds).

grading.pass: The build commits to a continuous/sustained audio strategy: (1) at least one looping/sustained layer running under gameplay (ambient/room-tone bed, looping or adaptive-stem music, drone, or steady tonal layer), NOT only discrete one-shots, AND (2) it is treated as a crafted continuous element with a deliberate role/length intended to play seamlessly underneath. Full marks add loop-seam integrity (zero-crossing cut on both channels, overlap-crossfaded so it doesn't click) and format/length discipline (OGG not MP3, ~15s+ ambient beds / ~6-10s steady sounds), ideally naming the MP3-padding click cause.
grading.partial: A continuous/looping/sustained layer is present and runs under gameplay, but the build says nothing about its seam integrity or its format/length discipline — the sustained-audio strategy exists but the craft of making the loop seamless is unaddressed.
grading.fail: The build's audio is a single non-looped clip played per event with NO continuous/sustained/looping layer of any kind — nothing persists underneath gameplay, so there is no loop to craft and no bed strategy at all.

criteria.change_reason: Original failed to discriminate: both MEAN and GREAT scored fail because the PASS gate demanded the narrow loop-SEAM specifics (zero-crossing, OGG-not-MP3, both-channels) that neither artifact enumerated — collapsing a build with a rich continuous-audio strategy (adaptive layered music whose stems crossfade by game state, plus ambient/reverb beds) to the same grade as a build with literally one non-looped clip per event. Rewrite lowers the PASS gate to the genuinely discriminating, always-present fact: does the build commit to ANY deliberately continuous/looping/sustained layer running under gameplay? The GREAT artifact's adaptive-stem music bed and ambient layers satisfy this; the MEAN artifact's single 2D non-looped clip per event provably does not (it has no sustained layer at all). The original seam/format/length craft is preserved intact as the full-marks ceiling, so the criterion still rewards real loop craft while now producing MEAN(fail) < GREAT(pass) instead of a non-discriminating fail/fail pair.

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — ENVIRONMENTAL ACOUSTICS ON A SHARED LISTENER/MASTER BUS. The world has acoustic identity: AudioReverb + AudioEqualizer applied ONCE on the listener-level/master bus (or a per-zone SoundGroup) and retuned/toggled as the listener enters a region — small room vs large hall vs cave vs outdoors — PLUS occlusion muffling behind geometry (low-pass/EQ cut, or engine acoustic simulation), rather than dry audio everywhere or a reverb instance spammed on every emitter. The discriminator is whether the build commits to per-space reverb+EQ at the bus level AND occlusion, NOT per-emitter effect spam. PASS requires the build to state (1) ONE reverb-per-space on the listener/master (a cave needs ONE reverb on the listener that activates when the listener enters the cave — not 40 reverb instances on 40 emitters), with parameters tuned per environment (small room ~0.5-1.5s decay, large hall ~2.5-4s, cave ~3-5s, balanced Wet/Dry) and zone detection (zone parts / Region / raycast) swapping it (legacy equivalent: SoundService.AmbientReverb ReverbType preset per zone, e.g. Hangar), AND (2) occlusion — audio muffled behind walls via an EQ/low-pass high-cut (or engine acoustic simulation with BOTH AudioListener and AudioEmitter AcousticSimulationEnabled=true, the subtle both-ends-flagged detail amateurs miss) and smoothly restored when clear. A build with no reverb (dead/dry, identical indoors vs outdoors) or a reverb instance stamped on every emitter FAILS. A build that commits to one shared-bus reverb-per-space tuned by zone AND occlusion muffling PASSES; smooth zone-transition blending, raycast/geometry-derived reverb parameters (decay/wet-dry from measured room size, flood-fill-averaged, modulated by distance/occlusion/angle), and engine diffraction (corner-bending) push toward full marks. A build with zone reverb but no occlusion (or occlusion but per-emitter reverb spam) earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: Generic audio applies no reverb at all (everything sounds dead/dry and identical indoors vs outdoors) or naively spams a reverb on every emitter — and it passes straight through walls at full volume so a sound on the far side of a building is as loud as if you stood next to it. Per-emitter effect spam is called out as the naive default that tanks performance and produces incoherent space; one reverb-per-space on the shared listener/master bus is 'the single biggest win in most projects' and the correct mental model (the ROOM reverberates, not each source) — both a massive perf win and the quality move, the audio analog of VFX role-separation done at the mix bus. Occlusion muffling behind geometry is one of the clearest perceptual upgrades and signals real audio engineering; engine acoustic simulation needs BOTH listener and emitter flagged or it silently does nothing. The ceiling is geometry-derived reverb (parameters from measured room size, smooth zone blends, modulated by distance/occlusion/angle) — 'precomputed environmental analysis replaces arbitrary parameters.' Grading the shared-bus-reverb-per-space-AND-occlusion commitment keeps this discriminating: a cave that echoes and walls that muffle clears it; a dry-everywhere or per-emitter-spam build cannot.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) AudioReverb + AudioEqualizer on the listener/master bus (or per-zone SoundGroup), tuned per environment (room ~0.5-1.5s / hall ~2.5-4s / cave ~3-5s decay, balanced Wet/Dry) and swapped by zone detection (zone parts / Region / raycast) — explicitly ONE reverb-per-space, not a reverb on every emitter — or the legacy SoundService.AmbientReverb ReverbType preset per zone, AND (2) occlusion muffling behind walls via EQ/low-pass high-cut (or engine acoustic simulation with BOTH AudioListener and AudioEmitter AcousticSimulationEnabled=true) restored smoothly when clear. Smooth zone-transition blending, raycast/geometry-derived reverb parameters modulated by distance/occlusion/angle, and engine diffraction are credited toward full marks. No reverb (dry everywhere) or a reverb stamped per-emitter does NOT satisfy this; zone reverb without occlusion, or occlusion with per-emitter reverb spam, earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Put ONE AudioReverb (+ AudioEqualizer) on the listener/master bus and retune it by zone (room/hall/cave/outdoor decay times) using zone parts or raycast detection — never 40 reverbs on 40 emitters; legacy: swap SoundService.AmbientReverb ReverbType per zone. Add occlusion: cast listener->source rays and cut highs (EQ low-pass) when blocked, restoring smoothly when clear — or enable engine acoustic simulation with AcousticSimulationEnabled=true on BOTH the listener AND every emitter.

grading.pass: The build commits to per-space reverb+EQ at the bus level AND occlusion: (1) ONE AudioReverb (+ AudioEqualizer) on the listener/master bus or a per-zone SoundGroup, tuned per environment (room ~0.5-1.5s / hall ~2.5-4s / cave ~3-5s decay, balanced Wet/Dry) and swapped by zone detection (zone parts / Region / raycast), or legacy SoundService.AmbientReverb ReverbType per zone — explicitly NOT a reverb per emitter, AND (2) occlusion muffling behind walls via EQ/low-pass high-cut (or engine acoustic simulation with BOTH AudioListener and AudioEmitter AcousticSimulationEnabled=true), restored smoothly when clear. Full marks add smooth zone-transition blending, raycast/geometry-derived reverb parameters modulated by distance/occlusion/angle, and engine diffraction.
grading.partial: Only one side holds: the build has zone-tuned shared-bus reverb but no occlusion, OR has occlusion muffling but applies reverb per-emitter (effect spam) instead of once on the listener/master bus.
grading.fail: No reverb at all (dead/dry, identical indoors vs outdoors), or a reverb instance stamped on every emitter with no shared-bus zone model and no occlusion.

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — ADAPTIVE LAYERED MUSIC (STEMS, NOT TRACK SWAPS). Music is decomposed into 4-8 synchronized STEMS (drums, bass, melody, tension pad, percussion) as separate looping AudioPlayers/Sounds started sample-aligned (all Play()'d within ONE frame / Heartbeat tick) and TimePosition-synced to a leader, each on its own AudioFader, with a state machine cross-fading per-stem volumes by a gameplay intensity value over a ~1.5s smoothing constant — instead of one looping track or a hard cut between explore.mp3 and combat.mp3. The discriminator is whether the build commits to sample-aligned stem layering with smoothed intensity-driven fades, NOT a single track or a hard swap. PASS requires the build to state (1) 4-8 independent looping stems started sample-aligned (same Heartbeat tick), each with its own AudioFader, re-synced against a leader to prevent drift, AND (2) a state machine driving per-stem fader volumes from a computed gameplay intensity (enemy proximity, recent damage) interpolated over a smoothing constant (~1.5s) so the mix never snaps or flickers (e.g. exploration: drums 0.2 / tension 0; combat: drums 1.0 / tension ramps in). A build that loops one music track unchanged, or hard-cuts between whole tracks on a state change, FAILS. A build that commits to sample-aligned stems + smoothed intensity-driven fades PASSES; the specific 1.5s flicker-prevention constant, drift re-sync against a leader stem, and event-marker-synced musical transitions push toward full marks. A build with stems that aren't sample-aligned (audible phasing), or intensity fades that snap with no smoothing, earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: Generic dynamic music is one looping track (predictable, unresponsive) or a hard cut from explore.mp3 to combat.mp3 — an audible jarring swap with no musical transition, and amateurs hard-switch on enemy proximity so intensity FLICKERS. Stem-based layering keeps one continuous bed and fades sub-mixes in/out by game state, so intensity tracks gameplay smoothly and adaptively — this is what AAA games do and is achievable on Roblox purely by wiring multiple library tracks (RoBeats won 2022 Best Audio Design on exactly this kind of system). The sample-aligned-same-frame start prevents phasing, and the ~1.5s smoothing constant specifically prevents the jarring intensity flicker. This is the highest-tier mixing move — the audio equivalent of VFX 'pelvis bias / idle breakers' polish — and pure curation+routing of library stems, not composition. Grading the sample-aligned-stems-AND-smoothed-intensity-fade commitment keeps this discriminating: a continuous bed that swells smoothly into combat clears it; a one-track loop or a hard track swap cannot.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) 4-8 independent looping stems (drums/bass/melody/tension/percussion) started sample-aligned within one frame/Heartbeat tick, each on its own AudioFader, TimePosition-re-synced to a leader to prevent drift, AND (2) a state machine driving per-stem fader volumes from a computed gameplay intensity, interpolated over a ~1.5s smoothing constant (e.g. explore: drums 0.2 / tension 0; combat: drums 1.0 / tension ramps). The explicit flicker-prevention smoothing constant, leader-stem drift re-sync, and event-marker-synced transitions are credited toward full marks. One looping track unchanged, or a hard cut between whole tracks, does NOT satisfy this; non-sample-aligned stems (phasing) or snapping un-smoothed intensity fades earn partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Split the music into 4-8 looping stems as separate AudioPlayers, Play() them all within one Heartbeat tick so they start sample-aligned, give each its own AudioFader, and re-sync TimePosition to a leader stem to stop drift — then drive each stem's fader volume from a computed gameplay-intensity value (enemy proximity, recent damage) interpolated over ~1.5s so combat swells in smoothly instead of hard-cutting from explore.mp3 to combat.mp3.

grading.pass: The build commits to sample-aligned stem layering with smoothed intensity-driven fades: (1) 4-8 independent looping stems started sample-aligned within one frame/Heartbeat tick, each on its own AudioFader, TimePosition-re-synced to a leader to prevent drift, AND (2) a state machine driving per-stem fader volumes from a computed gameplay intensity, interpolated over a ~1.5s smoothing constant (e.g. explore: drums 0.2 / tension 0; combat: drums 1.0 / tension ramps). Full marks add the explicit flicker-prevention smoothing constant, leader-stem drift re-sync, and event-marker-synced musical transitions.
grading.partial: The structure is present but flawed: stems are layered but not sample-aligned (audible phasing), OR the intensity-driven fades snap with no smoothing constant — one half of the sample-alignment-and-smoothing requirement is missing.
grading.fail: One music track is looped unchanged, or whole tracks are hard-cut on a state change (explore.mp3 -> combat.mp3) with no stem layering and no smoothed intensity fades.

criteria.statement: KILLER SYSTEM — A DEDICATED AMBIENCE / ENVIRONMENTAL-AUDIO SYSTEM (environmental sound treated as a first-class layer, not absent). The build has a deliberate environmental-audio system: a continuous ambience layer and/or environment-aware audio treatment that gives the world acoustic presence underneath the action SFX, rather than a soundscape that is ONLY discrete action clips with no environmental layer. The discriminator is whether the build commits to environmental/ambient audio as a designed dimension — a continuous ambience bed AND/OR space-aware treatment (reverb zones, environment-driven mix) — versus a build that has no environmental audio at all (silence between action sounds). PASS requires the build to state (1) a continuous ambience/environmental layer that is part of the design — an ambient bed and/or an environment-aware audio treatment (e.g. reverb zones / per-space acoustics applied to environmental audio) routed as a distinct ambience role — establishing that the WORLD has audio presence, not just the action, AND (2) that this is more than a single generic looping clip — it is composed (a bed plus other environmental elements, or space-tuned treatment) rather than one flat ambience loop. Crucially, the ceiling that earns full marks is true layered ambience CONSTRUCTION: a continuous low tonal/room-tone BED (30s+) UNDER many short foreground one-shots fired at randomized NON-repeating intervals, with context-specific clips that NAME the space (oven/order/chatter for a pizza parlor; crosswalk beeps for Tokyo) — and merely naming an 'Ambient' mixer bus with nothing behind it does NOT reach that ceiling. A build with NO environmental/ambience audio at all — only discrete action clips, dead silence otherwise — FAILS. A build that commits to a real ambience/environmental-audio layer (ambient bed and/or reverb-zone-treated environmental sound as a distinct role) PASSES; a layered bed UNDER randomized non-repeating foreground one-shots PLUS place-identifying clips push toward full marks. A build that gestures at environmental audio (an 'Ambient' bus, or one flat looping ambience clip) but neither constructs a bed+randomized-foreground layer nor applies space-aware treatment earns partial.
criteria.above_generic_rationale: The original criterion graded only the narrowest construction (a 30s+ bed UNDER randomized non-repeating place-naming one-shots) as its PASS gate, and explicitly disqualified the 'Ambient bus / reverb zone' mentions. Neither artifact named the full construction, so both scored fail and it separated nothing — even though one build commits to a real environmental-audio system (an Ambient bus role plus AudioReverb/AudioEcho + reverb zones + EQ occlusion giving the world acoustic identity) and the other has ZERO environmental audio (a single action clip per event, dead silence otherwise). The genuinely discriminating, always-present fact one tier down is whether the build treats environmental/ambient audio as a first-class layer AT ALL — a continuous ambience role and/or space-aware treatment — which is the structural precondition the full bed-plus-foreground construction sits on top of. A generic build has no world audio whatsoever; a real audio system always gives the environment presence. Making 'has a dedicated environmental/ambience layer (bed and/or reverb-zone treatment)' the PASS gate lets the strong artifact's ambience-bus-plus-reverb-zones commitment clear it while the silence-between-clips build cannot, and preserves the true layered-construction (bed + randomized non-repeating foreground + place-naming clips) as the full-marks ceiling.
criteria.evidence_required: A statement/dump showing (1) a continuous ambience/environmental audio layer that is part of the design — an ambient bed routed as a distinct ambience role AND/OR environment-aware audio treatment (reverb zones, per-space acoustics, EQ occlusion applied to environmental audio) giving the world acoustic presence — NOT a soundscape that is only discrete action clips with silence otherwise, AND (2) that it is more than one flat generic looping clip (a composed bed, multiple environmental elements, or space-tuned treatment). For full marks: true layered construction — a continuous low tonal/room-tone bed (30s+) UNDER many short foreground one-shots at randomized NON-repeating intervals — PLUS place-identifying clips that name the space (oven/order/chatter for a pizza parlor; crosswalk beeps for Tokyo); a three-layer tonal-bed + ambient-bed + foreground structure, time-of-day variation, and region-gated transitions (VolumetricAudio + zero rolloff) are also credited. A build with NO environmental/ambience audio at all (only action clips, dead silence) does NOT satisfy this and earns FAIL; gesturing at environmental audio via only an 'Ambient' bus name or one flat looping ambience clip — with neither a constructed bed+randomized foreground nor space-aware treatment — earns partial.
criteria.concrete_fix: Give the world its own audio presence instead of leaving silence between action sounds: add a dedicated ambience/environmental layer — at minimum a continuous ambient bed routed as its own role and/or space-aware treatment (reverb zones, per-space acoustics) so the environment sounds like a place. Then build it up properly: a continuous low tonal/room-tone bed (30s+ loop) UNDER many short foreground one-shots (e.g. bird calls, wind/rustle variants) fired at randomized non-repeating intervals so no two minutes match, using context-specific clips that NAME the space (oven/order cues for a pizza parlor, crosswalk beeps for Tokyo) rather than one flat generic loop or merely an 'Ambient' mixer bus.

grading.pass: The build commits to a real environmental/ambience-audio layer: (1) a continuous ambience role (ambient bed) AND/OR environment-aware treatment (reverb zones / per-space acoustics / EQ occlusion on environmental audio) giving the world acoustic presence, NOT just discrete action clips with silence otherwise, AND (2) it is more than one flat generic looping clip (composed bed, multiple elements, or space-tuned treatment). Full marks add true layered construction — a 30s+ tonal/room-tone bed UNDER randomized NON-repeating foreground one-shots — PLUS place-identifying clips that name the space, and may add a three-layer structure, time-of-day variation, and region-gated transitions (VolumetricAudio + zero rolloff).
grading.partial: The build gestures at environmental audio but thinly: it names an 'Ambient' mixer bus, or uses one flat generic looping ambience clip, with NEITHER a constructed bed-under-randomized-non-repeating-foreground layer NOR genuine space-aware treatment (reverb zones / per-space acoustics) behind it — an ambience role acknowledged but not built out.
grading.fail: The build has NO environmental/ambience audio at all — only discrete action clips, with dead silence between them — so the world has no audio presence of any kind: no bed, no ambient role, no reverb-zone / space-aware treatment.

criteria.change_reason: Original failed to discriminate: both MEAN and GREAT scored fail because the PASS gate demanded the full narrow construction (30s+ bed UNDER randomized non-repeating place-naming one-shots) AND explicitly disqualified the very things the GREAT artifact stated ('Ambient' bus role, reverb zones, EQ occlusion) — collapsing a build with a genuine environmental-audio system to the same grade as a build with zero environmental audio (one action clip per event, dead silence otherwise). Rewrite lowers the PASS gate to the genuinely discriminating, always-present fact: does the build treat environmental/ambient audio as a first-class layer at all — a continuous ambience role AND/OR space-aware treatment (reverb zones, per-space acoustics)? The GREAT artifact's Ambient bus plus AudioReverb/AudioEcho + reverb zones + EQ occlusion satisfies this; the MEAN artifact's single 2D action clip with no ambience provably does not. The true bed-plus-randomized-non-repeating-foreground construction and place-naming clips are preserved as the full-marks ceiling (and a bare 'Ambient' bus name with nothing behind it is held to partial, not pass), so the criterion now produces MEAN(fail) < GREAT(pass) instead of a non-discriminating fail/fail pair.
